brief.industry_meta: Edge AI Infrastructure · Modular, Satellite-Connected Data Centres
brief.deck: Armada, the San Francisco builder of ruggedised, satellite-connected data centres that run on oil fields, mines and Navy sites, closed an oversubscribed $230M Series B at a $2B pre-money valuation on 19 May 2026 and will build them at a new Arizona factory with Johnson Controls from this summer.
brief.the_case_p1: On 19 May 2026 Armada announced a $230M oversubscribed Series B at a $2B pre-money valuation, co-led by Overmatch, BlackRock and 8090 Industries, taking total funding to nearly $500M. Johnson Controls invested alongside an agreement to build Galleon Forge One, an up-to-400,000 sq ft Arizona factory with more than 500 jobs, in continuous production from summer 2026. The company says customer bookings grew 540% from FY25 to FY26. Its Galleon and Leviathan units are self-contained, Starlink-connected data centres for places with no grid or fibre: oil fields, mines, ships and bases.
brief.the_case_p2: The grid has already bought the data-centre archetype: Core Scientific joined Cadillac as official data-centre partner in March 2026, CoreWeave sits at Aston Martin, Hewlett Packard Enterprise at Mercedes. None of them sells compute that travels. A Formula 1 garage is a temporary remote site rebuilt 24 times a year, which is the problem Armada was founded to solve, and Microsoft's M12 and Johnson Controls are investor names a team can put on a car.
brief.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  The round closed on 19 May and Galleon Forge One starts production this summer, so the brand story and the budget crest together. The United States GP in Austin (October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) are the American stages left in 2026, and teams settle 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter.
brief.why_team_para: Haas is the American-owned privateer of the grid, built by a machine-tool manufacturer, and its technology roster is connectivity and services: CommScope as Official Connectivity Partner, Ruckus Networks for trackside networking, Mphasis for digital services. No compute, cloud or data-centre partner is listed. Armada's units plug in behind the network Ruckus already runs, so the fit is complementary: two American industrial brands, one Arizona factory, Austin as the launch stage.
brief.value_section_label: VALUE TO TGR HAAS F1 TEAM
brief.value_content: MODE A - operational. Each race weekend the team rebuilds a remote site: a garage of compute for telemetry, video and strategy, in a car park in Baku or a paddock in Las Vegas. A ruggedised Galleon in the freight, with Starlink backhaul managed by Armada's software, gives Haas a garage data centre that works before the circuit's fibre does, plus edge inference on the factory-to-track link. In return: Austin and Las Vegas hospitality for Armada's energy and government buyers.
brief.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official Edge Computing Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, 2027-2029, across the Arizona ramp and a probable listing window. Estimated $2-4M a year, part-payable in equipment and managed services. Scope: sidepod or halo placement, a Galleon in the garage, US-race hospitality, engineering content built on the freight-to-pit-wall story.
brief.decision_maker_bio: Wright co-founded Armada in late 2022 after running DataRobot as CEO and AppDynamics as COO through its $3.7B sale to Cisco; he fronts every raise and the Johnson Controls deal. Path: Jon Runyan, Co-Founder and COO, ex-Okta general counsel. No chief marketing officer is listed.
brief.opening_angle_intro: Lead with the garage as a remote site.
brief.opening_angle_quote: “Dan, you build data centres for places with no fibre and no grid. A Formula 1 garage is that place 24 times a year, and the American privateer has no compute partner. 25 minutes before Austin to price a Galleon in the freight?”
score_cells: Round closed 19 May; Arizona production from summer; Austin and Las Vegas in window.
$230M raise at $2B pre-money; nearly $500M raised; marketing budget still modest.
American-built AI infrastructure for hard places; industrial customer base.
Rivals hold data-centre lanes at three teams; no hard deadline beyond Q4 rosters.
MODE A: a travelling garage data centre with satellite backhaul.
risks: A $2B company with no marketing chief; a multi-million F1 fee competes with factory capital.
Size the entry at the Haas price point; structure part of it as equipment and managed services.
Ruckus and CommScope hold connectivity at Haas; Armada manages Starlink terminals, which the team could read as the same lane.
Define the category as edge compute and satellite backhaul, and clear it with Haas before the first call.
brief.bottom_line: A $230M round at $2B pre-money, a factory in production this summer and a product that is literally a data centre for remote sites give Armada budget, story and a real garage workstream at once. The compute lane at the American privateer is open and two US races remain inside the window.

why_now.label: Trigger
why_now.text: On 19 May 2026 Armada announced a $230M oversubscribed Series B at a $2B pre-money valuation, co-led by Overmatch, BlackRock and 8090 Industries, taking total funding to nearly $500M. The figures come from the company's own release and were carried by CNBC the same day.

why_now.label: A factory, not just a round
why_now.text: Johnson Controls invested alongside an agreement to build Galleon Forge One, an up-to-400,000 sq ft Arizona factory with more than 500 jobs, in continuous production from summer 2026, initially building the megawatt-scale Leviathan. A company that has just committed to American manufacturing has a story it needs to tell to customers, policymakers and future public-market investors, and a race in Austin is where that audience gathers.

why_now.label: Demand is the proof point
why_now.text: The company reports 540% customer bookings growth from FY25 to FY26 and a 2,000% year-on-year rise in Q1 FY27 bookings; these are company figures, unaudited, and the brief treats them as such. Customers named in its own releases span oil and gas, mining, telecom, hospitality and government, including the U.S. Navy, Alaska's Department of Transportation, Targa Resources and Atlas Energy.

why_now.label: Calendar window
why_now.text: The Miami GP has just run; the United States GP in Austin (October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) are the American rounds left in 2026, and teams settle their 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. A deal agreed over the summer can be announced at Austin and activated in full for 2027.

why_team.label: The open lane
why_team.text: The Haas roster is connectivity and services: Toyota Gazoo Racing as title partner, Haas Automation, MoneyGram, CommScope as Official Connectivity Partner (Feb 2025), Ruckus Networks as Official Networking Partner (Jan 2026), Mphasis as Official Digital Partner, UChicago Medicine and Infobip. No compute, cloud or data-centre partner is listed, so Official Edge Computing Partner is a clean category at the most accessible price on the grid.

why_team.label: Complementary, not a clash
why_team.text: CommScope and Ruckus run the wired and wireless network in the garage, pit wall and hospitality. Armada's Galleon is the compute and the satellite backhaul that sit behind that network. The clash-check is a category definition, not a rival product, and it should be cleared with Haas before the first call.

why_team.label: Two American industrial brands
why_team.text: Haas is the American-owned privateer of the grid, founded by a machine-tool manufacturer. Armada is building an Arizona factory with Johnson Controls to make AI infrastructure in the United States. The shared story, American industry that builds hard things, is one the team can tell in Austin and Las Vegas without stretching.

why_team.label: A team that will use the product
why_team.text: A privateer with a lean budget gains most from equipment it would not otherwise buy. A garage data centre that works before the circuit's fibre is connected, and edge inference for the link between the factory and the track, is consumed on race weekends rather than displayed on the car.

value.label: Operational workstream (Mode A)
value.text: Every race weekend the team rebuilds a remote site: a garage full of compute for telemetry, video and strategy, in a car park in Baku or a paddock in Las Vegas. A ruggedised Galleon travelling in the freight, with Starlink backhaul managed by Armada's software, gives Haas a garage data centre that works before the circuit's fibre does, plus edge inference on the factory-to-track link, and a hot spare for the circuit connection when it fails.

value.label: Commercial lift for the team
value.text: Armada sells to energy, mining, defence and government buyers. Its guest list at Austin and Las Vegas is the industrial and public-sector audience that Haas's other B2B partners want in the suite, and a partner that can bring a Navy or Department of Transportation customer to the paddock changes the hospitality mix.

value.label: Content and ecosystem
value.text: The freight-to-pit-wall story is filmable: a data centre in a container, unloaded on Thursday, live by Friday. Co-produced engineering content with the team's trackside IT group, a reference customer for Armada's enterprise sales, and a factory story that runs from Arizona to the garage.

value.label: What the team gives back
value.text: Official Edge Computing Partner designation, sidepod or halo placement, a Galleon branded in the garage, hospitality at Austin and Las Vegas, driver and engineering access for Armada's channels, and a case study the team's Official Digital Partner can co-sign.

ruled_out.reason: Core Scientific is official data-centre partner (Mar 2026) and TWG AI is primary and exclusive AI partner; the natural American alternative is taken in this lane.
CoreWeave, Official AI Cloud Computing Partner since May 2025, holds the compute lane.
Hewlett Packard Enterprise, AMD and Microsoft cover infrastructure, silicon and cloud.
Oracle is title partner and the cloud incumbent.
Dell Technologies, Google Cloud and Groq occupy hardware, cloud and inference compute.
HP (title), IBM and DXC Technology cover compute hardware, cloud and IT services.

ruled_out.team: Atlassian Williams Racing · Visa Cash App Racing Bulls · Audi Revolut F1 Team
ruled_out.reason: Open in this lane but not chosen: none carries the American industrial story that pairs Armada's Arizona factory with the Haas identity; Williams (VAST, Claude) is data-native but British-led, Audi is German-led.

extended.ask: A 25-minute call with Dan Wright before the United States GP to confirm the category definition against the Ruckus and CommScope agreements, agree an Austin announcement window, and size an Official Edge Computing Partner entry against the Haas 2027 roster.

# Armada → TGR Haas F1 Team — verification log (N° 218, issued for 19 May 2026)

Built in-session on 6 Sep 2026 at no API cost (no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the sandbox) from a case spec
(`armada.case.json`) with Claude doing the research, verification and writing; the calendar table,
sponsor table, 13-rule audit and the 2-page render ran as code via `python -m intel.session_case`.
The row came from a thin scan dated 19 May 2026 (score 87, no team); every fact was re-verified live
and the score re-set honestly.

**Sandbox limitation, stated plainly:** direct fetches of armada.ai, prnewswire.com, cnbc.com,
theorg.com, geekwire.com, pulse2.com, research.contrary.com and finance.yahoo.com were blocked by the
egress proxy. Each claim below was checked against the search summary of the primary page named as
the evidence URL (the company release text is quoted in several mirrors, which agree). Treat every
VERIFIED line as REPORTED until a person opens the link. Confidence is MEDIUM and the footer reads
VERIFY BEFORE CIRCULATION.

Pulse 2.0) and CNBC's same-day report agree: **$230M oversubscribed Series B at a $2B pre-money
valuation**, co-led by Overmatch, BlackRock and 8090 Industries; total funding nearly $500M; a
Johnson Controls investment alongside the **Galleon Forge One** agreement (up to 400,000 sq ft,
Arizona, 500+ jobs, continuous production from summer 2026, Leviathan first). The trigger date is
the row date, inside the 90-day window. The thin row's trigger text was accurate.

## Decision path

Dan Wright (Co-Founder & CEO) fronts every raise and the Johnson Controls deal and is the sponsorship

leadership listing found; John Zissimos appears on The Org only as "Advisor, Launch CMO and Brand
Architect", so the brief does not name a CMO. No CFO is listed either.

- **No motorsport tie found** for Wright, Runyan, Nair or Mishra after searching; `leadership_ties`

- **No revenue figure** is used: none is public. The bookings-growth percentages are the company's
